title: Avoiding Double Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drain Lines
description: A frequent error in horizontal waste pipe installation is using a double sanitary tee to join opposite fixture drains into a horizontal run. Sanitary tees are designed for vertical-to-horizontal transitions or vent connections, not horizontal flow consolidation. When solids and wastewater flow across a double tee on a horizontal plane, waste from one side can crossover into the opposing pipe rather than directing downstream. This causes frequent blockages, improper venting performance, and poor drainage velocity. Always use a double combination wye and eighth bend or appropriate directional fittings on horizontal runs as required by code.

Avoiding Double Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drain Lines

A frequent error in horizontal waste pipe installation is using a double sanitary tee to join opposite fixture drains into a horizontal run. Sanitary tees are designed for vertical-to-horizontal transitions or vent connections, not horizontal flow consolidation. When solids and wastewater flow across a double tee on a horizontal plane, waste from one side can crossover into the opposing pipe rather than directing downstream. This causes frequent blockages, improper venting performance, and poor drainage velocity. Always use a double combination wye and eighth bend or appropriate directional fittings on horizontal runs as required by code.
